thread:
Sam Turner: Heads up — multiple orgs (≈50) reporting $0 or NaN on the Token Cost dashboard starting ~03:00 UTC. Example: org_93b shows tokens=0 and cost=NaN on daily rollup. Filed customer ticket #CSS-4821.
Priya Nair: Are these only subaccounts or top-level orgs? any pattern (region/model)?
Sam Turner: Mixed. ~70% EU region. Quick ad-hoc SQL shows ledger join returning NULL for price for certain model rows. Also seeing a column 'kv_snapshot_id' present.
Jorge Alvarez: I pulled service logs — the rollup-grouper job that aggregates hourly -> daily failed a retry during KV snapshotting at 02:58:12. Suspect the grouper wrote a partial snapshot (size 0) that later jobs read.
Sam Turner: paste of minimal repro query and sample rows:
```sql
SELECT org_id, model, timestamp, tokens, price_per_token
FROM token_rollups_daily
WHERE org_id = 'org_93b'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
Returned rows:
| org_id  | model               | timestamp           | tokens | price_per_token |
| org_93b | redwood-embed-v1    | 2026-03-17 02:00:00 | 0      | NULL           |
| org_93b | redwood-embed-v1    | 2026-03-17 01:00:00 | 1234   | 0.0001         |
Priya Nair: NULL price explains NaN downstream. Do we have a fallback price lookup? Shouldn't price be joined from price_catalog with default?
Jorge Alvarez: Normally yes. The grouper was supposed to enrich with latest price from price_catalog at snapshot time. I see an error earlier: `KVSnapshotError: snapshot sequence mismatch (expected 1242 got 1241)` and then `Grouper: partial write completed`.
infra-bot: deploy-ops triggered: rollup-grouper v2.3.1 rolled back at 02:59:47 (reason: partial snapshot).
Elaine Chen: Is this affecting compute-only (no price) rows or is price nullable for certain model versions? Could be a recent price_catalog schema change.
Priya Nair: I checked price_catalog migration — no schema changes this week. More likely the snapshot read returned an older/empty shard for some orgs due to the mismatch.
Sam Turner: Customers are seeing incorrect bill previews and CSV exports with $0. I already replied to the escalated customer: "we're investigating; will backfill and re-run rollups".
Jorge Alvarez: Plan: 1) re-run grouper for the affected hourly window (02:00-03:00) with strict snapshot verification flag; 2) run backfill job to rebuild daily rollups for affected orgs; 3) push a soft-fix in dashboard to treat NULL price as last-known-price until backfill completes.
onchalant note: commands I'm going to run:
```
# replay grouper with snapshot strictness
./bin/rollup-grouper replay --start 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z --end 2026-03-17T03:00:00Z --verify-snapshot
# backfill example for org_93b
./bin/backfill_token_costs --org org_93b --from 2026-03-01 --to 2026-03-17
```
Priya Nair: +1. Also add a cheap guard in the dashboard: if cost is NaN/NULL show "Recomputing" rather than $0 — customers keep assuming free credits.
oncall-sre: I've claimed this oncall. Running replay now, will monitor job logs and OpenSearch metrics for retries.
Jorge Alvarez: Job started, logs show snapshot verify step failing for two shards (eu-west-1a/kv-3). I'm escalating to storage team to check KV snapshotter (possible race during compact).
Elaine Chen: For comms — please prepare a short customer note: what happened, which orgs, ETA for backfill. Sam, can you list top 10 affected org IDs?
Sam Turner: Yup, compiling list and adding to ticket. Preliminary: org_93b, org_29f, org_5aa, org_7c3, org_44d, org_88e, org_101g, org_12h, org_77z, org_66y.
Priya Nair: Once backfill succeeds, I'll run a QC check: compare token sums for last 7 days vs pre-incident snapshot and confirm price enrichment. If mismatch <0.2% we can close.
Sam Turner: Thanks team. I'll ping customers with tentative ETA 4 hours and update #support-status. :eyes:
